title: Parivaar Express Brings Tiffins, Snacks and Pastries to Hampden Township
excerpt: The quick-service Indian restaurant opened October 12 at 65 Gateway Drive in the Gateway Square Shopping Center, specializing in tiffins — packed lunches — plus afternoon snacks and pastries.
body:
• Parivaar Express opened on October 12 at 65 Gateway Drive in the Gateway Square Shopping Center in Hampden Township, Cumberland County.
  • Beyond chicken tikka masala and curries, the restaurant specializes in tiffins — packed lunches — and in afternoon snacks and pastries, according to PennLive.
  • The quick-service restaurant offers dine-in, takeout and catering; its own site lists the Mechanicsburg address as 65 Gateway Drive and the phone number as (717) 802-7478.
  • Parivaar — the Hindi word for family — is a name already known in Mechanicsburg, where menu listings for Parivaar show a deep bench of Andhra and Chettinad dishes and desserts such as gulab jamun, rasmalai and kulfi.

A new Indian restaurant in Hampden Township is betting that lunch, not just dinner, is where it can stand out. Parivaar Express opened on October 12 at 65 Gateway Drive in the Gateway Square Shopping Center, serving the familiar chicken tikka masala and curries alongside a specialty that most local Indian restaurants do not build around: tiffins, the packed lunches eaten across India at work, at school and on trains, plus afternoon snacks and pastries, according to PennLive.

More Than Tikka Masala

PennLive’s Sue Gleiter reported ahead of the opening that Parivaar Express “will dish out more than traditional chicken tikka masala and curries,” with tiffins, afternoon snacks and pastries as the specialties. That mix points the restaurant at three different dayparts: a packed-lunch trade at midday, a snack-and-tea trade in the afternoon, and a conventional curry dinner trade in the evening. It is a broader brief than the standard suburban Indian menu, and it matches how the restaurant describes itself: an Indian quick-service restaurant built, in its own words, around “flavors of home, speed of today.”

The Tiffin Idea

A tiffin is a packed meal, traditionally carried in stacked metal containers, and the word covers both the lunch itself and the break at which it is eaten. For Indian professionals and students in central Pennsylvania, a tiffin offer is the closest a restaurant can come to a home kitchen on a workday: rice, a curry or dal, a vegetable and bread, packed to go. Building a menu around tiffins, afternoon snacks and pastries therefore targets the diaspora’s weekday routine rather than only its weekend restaurant meals — and gives non-Indian diners in the Gateway Square area a fast, inexpensive way into the cuisine at lunch.

A Family Kitchen, Run for Speed

The restaurant’s own website leans on the same contrast. It describes dishes “prepared fresh each morning using whole spices and seasonal ingredients,” a menu “rooted in generations of home cooking,” and service designed to be fast, with dine-in, takeout and catering for weddings, corporate lunches and family parties. The name is the pitch: parivaar means family, and the Express format is meant to deliver family-style cooking at quick-service speed.

The Parivaar name already carries a menu history in Mechanicsburg. Menu listings for Parivaar published by AllMenus run well beyond the standard curry-house list, with Andhra chicken curry cooked with coconut and poppy seeds, gongura chicken with red sorrel leaves, Chettinad goat curry, and a run of biryanis, as well as desserts including gajar ka halwa, rasmalai, rice kheer, gulab jamun and kulfi, mostly priced between $7.99 and $13.99 on that listing. Readers should treat those listings as background on the kitchen’s range rather than as Parivaar Express’s confirmed opening menu, which PennLive summarized as tikka masala, curries, tiffins, snacks and pastries.

Part of a Growing Corridor

Parivaar Express joins a dense cluster of Indian restaurants in the Harrisburg suburbs, several of them along or near the Carlisle Pike in Hampden Township and Mechanicsburg. For Cumberland County’s growing Indian community, the pattern matters more than any single opening: the corridor now supports not just full-service curry houses but specialized formats — in this case, a quick-service shop organized around the packed lunch. That is the kind of business a diaspora sustains only when it is large enough to eat its own food on ordinary weekdays, not just on occasions.

Visiting

Parivaar Express is at 65 Gateway Drive, Suite B-102 in the Gateway Square Shopping Center, Hampden Township, with a Mechanicsburg, PA 17050 address. Its website lists the phone number as (717) 802-7478 and offers dine-in, takeout and catering. PennLive did not name the owners in the coverage available for this report, and the restaurant’s website does not name them either; readers looking for opening-week hours should confirm them by phone, as new restaurants commonly adjust hours in their first weeks.
